subject: general
question: Why is the biodiversity of the Lakshadweep Islands less than that of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands?

options.text: Smaller land area and lack of forest areas

solution:
The correct answer is __**Smaller land area and lack of forest areas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The biodiversity of a region depends on several factors, including **geography, climate, soil, and vegetation**.
 
• The **Lakshadweep Islands** are geographically smaller in size compared to the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**. Due to their smaller land area, they inherently support a limited variety of flora and fauna.
 
• The **Lakshadweep Islands** lack significant forested areas compared to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, which are covered with dense tropical forests. Forests provide habitats for diverse species, and their absence in Lakshadweep limits the biodiversity in these islands.
 
• The **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**, on the other hand, are larger and have a more diverse range of ecosystems, including tropical rainforests, mangroves, and coral reefs, which support a wider variety of species.
 
• The geographical isolation of the Lakshadweep Islands further limits the migration of species, reducing biodiversity compared to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• Thus, the smaller land area and lack of forest areas are the primary reasons for the lower biodiversity in the Lakshadweep Islands compared to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. *Hence, the correct answer is "Smaller land area and lack of forest areas".*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lakshadweep Islands:**

 
 
• The Lakshadweep Islands are a group of 36 small islands located in the **Arabian Sea**, off the southwestern coast of India.
 
• These islands are primarily composed of **coral atolls, reefs, and sandbars**, with very limited land area and vegetation.
 
• The soil in Lakshadweep is sandy and not very fertile, which limits the growth of forest vegetation and reduces the habitat available for terrestrial species.
 
• The biodiversity of Lakshadweep is primarily marine, with vibrant coral reefs and a variety of aquatic species, but terrestrial biodiversity is relatively low.
 
 
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands:**
 
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are located in the **Bay of Bengal** and consist of around 572 islands. They have a total land area of approximately **8,249 square kilometers**, much larger than Lakshadweep.
 
• These islands have extensive **tropical rainforests**, mangroves, and a rich diversity of flora and fauna. The dense forest cover provides a habitat for many endemic species.
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are home to numerous terrestrial animals, including **Andaman wild pigs, Nicobar megapodes, and saltwater crocodiles**, as well as aquatic biodiversity.
 
• The geographical location of these islands, along with their larger land area and varied ecosystems, makes them a hotspot for biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Factors affecting biodiversity:**
 
 
• Important factors influencing biodiversity include **climatic conditions, availability of resources, geographical size, and habitat diversity.**
 
• Regions with larger land areas, diverse ecosystems, and favorable climates tend to support higher biodiversity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison between Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar Islands:**

 
 
• The **Lakshadweep Islands** are much smaller in size, with a total land area of around **32 square kilometers**, compared to the larger Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• The **climate** of the Lakshadweep Islands is tropical but more uniform, while the Andaman and Nicobar Islands have a mix of tropical and subtropical climates, providing a variety of habitats.
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are part of the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot, which is one of the **36 global biodiversity hotspots** recognized for their rich flora and fauna.
 
• In contrast, the Lakshadweep Islands are not part of any recognized biodiversity hotspots, which is another factor for their lower biodiversity levels.
